1.explanation: By using the `type="filterable"` prop on `MultiSelect` and giving it a fixed `id`, Carbon’s implementation assigns that same `id` to both the outer ListBoxField <div> and the inner <input>. When you click to open the menu, each option is rendered as a <div role="option"> but the container is a <div role="group"> rather than <div role="listbox">, so DAP flags them. Likewise, the duplicate id on the wrapper and the input triggers the “id must be unique” violation. Running this code in Storybook or a local React app with the DAP scanner enabled will reproduce both accessibility errors.
1.bug_scenario: When you render a filterable MultiSelect (type="filterable") and pass in an explicit id, Carbon injects the same id onto both the outer ListBoxField wrapper <div> and the internal <input>. When the menu is open, each option is rendered as a <div role="option"> but its parent container does not have role="listbox", so DAP flags each option as not contained in a listbox. Finally, because both the wrapper <div> and the <input> share the same id, DAP reports “Element ‘id’ attribute values must be unique”. The screenshot shows these two issues in the Storybook iframe: duplicate id errors and “option” elements not in a listbox.
